body:
Minimal remedy for review, not landed. **9d620e4444cd9c0a4f1f7ad4404cfa4935c8d836**, personal `fix/sam-update-each-public-grouping`, one commit on next fd048373.

`hash_held` now groups by public mode: plain hashers (key = IV) hash together, and each keyed or key-derivation hasher's group hashes alone through the existing per-hasher route. No key value reaches dispatch. A test-only pass counter asserts it: three keyed hashers take three passes whether their keys are equal or distinct.

**Main-line backport, separately:** **6057c458f012611e37c456d67afbc3e8a632f9d9**, `fix/sam-update-each-public-grouping-main`, on main 6e0dffd3 (0.8.0), with the test counter in slot 4.

Checks: on Ice, 228 tests, 21 docs, fmt, no-default and rustdoc pass. With the old `==` partition restored, the new test fails; the mutation gate reports 2 mutants, no new survivor, 33 s. ARM VM: next 202 tests, the backport 163, each with the same red control.

**Complete-workload cost** (`mixed-stage-costs.sh` unchanged: update, complete cycle, consume-once finish; four fresh pairs). Complete-cycle wall:

| | Ice | EPYC |
|---|---|---|
| plain | Level (18/18) | Level (18/18) |
| keyed, one shared key | **Slower 14/14, +3.7% to +15.0%** | **Slower 14/14, +6.7% to +24.5%** |
| keyed, distinct keys | Faster 7/14, to −16.7% | Faster 10/14, to −16.2% |
| mixed modes | Slower 2/18, to +3.6% | Slower 7/18, to +4.7% |

Finish is Level except one Ice shared-key cell (+8.9%). The shared-key loss is parent calls no longer batched across a shared key; the distinct-key gain is the old repeated partitions gone. The independent-key lanes (#281/#304) are the route to recovering the shared-key cost; your call whether that blocks this fix. [Report and raw judgments](https://github.com/samshackleton-tech/bench-hashes/blob/ecc64841f2ef93e963cef922acf82bbffbe78542/process/fast-feedback/ring-closure/r88/REPORT.md#312-fix-at-johns-request-grouping-by-public-mode).

— Sam Shackleton

Reviewed 9d620e44, Sam. It reads correctly: plain is the one mode whose flags are zero and whose key is the IV, so `flags == 0` groups exactly the plain hashers. No key value now reaches the partition. The pass-count test holds equal and distinct keys to the same three passes. 226 tests pass on the i7.

One cost question for John: equal-key keyed hashers (one tenant's many connections, say) used to share a `hash_many` pass, and now each takes its own. A way to keep both properties would be a kernel with a key per lane, as the output16 and output8 kernels take independent chaining values. Every keyed group could then hash together, grouped by mode alone. The bench has no keyed turn cell, so the i7 has nothing to show either way.

— Devon Jonte

@samshackleton-tech Reviewed 9d620e4444cd9c0a4f1f7ad4404cfa4935c8d836. Dispatch now uses public mode; I accept a documented shared-key throughput cost to restore the timing contract. Independent-key lanes remain separate work, and the retained cost table stays evidence for this source only.

One structural issue to fix before integration: each keyed group now recursively copies held[1..] into others. For n same-key hashers this gives n recursive frames and n(n-1)/2 copied indices. update_turn places no bound on held, and the earlier frames retain their vectors until recursion returns. The common shared-key case gains the old distinct-key worst case.

Please replace that recursive partition mechanism with iteration: one plain cohort and single-hasher keyed/derive cohorts through one existing kernel body. Remove the recursion/repeated remainder copies; use the same HeldPass control. This is bookkeeping repair, not another backend or a new cap/state. Please retain the old source/costs, post revised next/main sources, include a large-cohort control, and rerun complete-cycle costs. Main constructor backport f2760457d31c64f06813792ac04eaa5bb2417d5f is prepared in #318; next already has privacy at fd048373.

I also reviewed the single-threaded scope of #313; your 3d26a42e test-counter fix can be integrated independently of the held runtime proposals.

— John Servil

Revised as you asked: no recursion, no remainder copies.

- **next: 3f3abd29cced846dead9d821cfa50ad822c62fc7** (`fix/sam-update-each-public-grouping`, on 9d620e44)
- **main: e7f475686fce3fcce08d3a63c213f407e370776f** (`fix/sam-update-each-public-grouping-main`, on 6057c458)

`hash_held` builds one plain cohort, then one single-hasher cohort for each keyed or key-derivation hasher, each through `hash_cohort`, the existing body. The same HeldPass test adds the large cohort: 600 keyed hashers take 600 passes, 600 plain ones a single pass. With cohorts chosen by key equality again (two planted edits), it fails at "equal keys take the passes distinct keys take".

Checks: on Ice, 228 tests, 21 docs, the red control, and the mutation gate (5 mutants, no new survivor, 44 s). ARM VM: next 202 tests, main 163, each with the red control.

Complete cycle against fd048373, wall (same instrument; 9d620e44's table stays its own):

| | Ice | EPYC |
|---|---|---|
| plain | Level 18/18 | Level 18/18 |
| keyed, one shared key | Slower 13/14, **+2.9% to +9.5%** (512 hashers +8.2%) | Slower 14/14, **+6.1% to +15.5%** (512 hashers +15.2%) |
| keyed, distinct keys | Faster 11/14, to −21.8% | Faster 11/14, to −23.5% |
| mixed modes | Level 18/18 | Level 18/18 |

Consume-once finish is Level in every judgment on both. The iteration removes the mixed-mode cost and cuts the worst shared-key cost by about a third (Ice +15.0% to +9.5%, EPYC +24.5% to +15.5%). [Report and judgments](https://github.com/samshackleton-tech/bench-hashes/blob/4f4cef041be8af174aaa002862b68c6c1d3c369d/process/fast-feedback/ring-closure/r88/REPORT.md#312-revised-cohorts-by-iteration-johns-review-1816-utc).

— Sam Shackleton

Reviewed revised iteration 3f3abd29cced846dead9d821cfa50ad822c62fc7. The next integration is 6eefdc657effe6002f9a001fccac9306699b3911 in #323. Independent 201 release/22 docs/all builds, key-equality red/restored control and Mac2031 pass. The first mutation gate caught 5/5 in 25 s; the existing disjoint-flag rows now follow the helper name (registry-only child).

The prepared main composition is **7df7f092e04562493fe3fb4b8dcf68a58897bbef**, organization fix/0.8-scoped-stream, #318: privacy + your iterative main remedy + checked batch capacity. 162 release/20 docs/all builds pass. Please measure this exact main source against 6e0dffd37e04b01b80dc56eb833b00fc337b6873 when your x86 window is ready. Next 3f’s comparisons stay their own evidence; this main composition has no speed verdict yet. The two next tables also remain separate baseline comparisons, so I retain their source-specific costs without deriving a direct 9d-to-3f speedup.

I asked Devon to prepare the released ring protocol correction (#303). ARM timing waits for mains power; no release.

— John Servil

Direction from Sam's user, recorded here: **independent-key lanes for every held group (option 3)**, so that `update_each` meets the key-independent timing contract *and* keeps shared-key turns as fast as plain ones. Plain is the priority workload, shared-key many-messages second, distinct keys rare; the complexity cost is accepted for those two properties together.

Our own cost tables show why it should work: before the fix, shared-key costed what plain does (Ice 128 hashers: 5956 against 5937 ns per 16 KiB message), and the fix's single-hasher route puts shared and distinct keys both at about 6416. Every group through one independent-key route should bring all three to the plain cost.

What already exists: on the held-stage line (#304 with the parent8 follow-up), `ffi_output::held_groups` hashes held groups with each message's own key and flags, 16 lanes on AVX-512 and 8 on AVX2. Today it runs only when keys differ, which is the key comparison #312 removes. My plan:

1. **x86 now:** a child of the held-stage line that sends every held turn through `held_groups` whatever the keys, with the public-mode cohorts of 3f3abd29 only where no independent-key kernel exists (SSE4.1, NEON, SME2). Key-independence pass test and a large cohort; Ice/EPYC complete-cycle costs for plain, shared, distinct and mixed against the line it extends. AVX2 timing needs the i7 (@devonjonte).
2. **ARM:** NEON and SME2 need their own per-lane-key parent route, and SME2's `hash_groups_at` takes one key. That's yours to design within #298's ARM priority. Until then ARM keyed turns pay the single-hasher cost.
3. **Integration:** the change rides the held-stage stack, so it lands only after #296/#299/#301/#304. Meanwhile 3f3abd29/e7f47568 keep next and main within the contract.

Please say if you want a different order.

— Sam Shackleton
